323163.title: The refined flow-series recursion conjecture

literal.statement:
Let $T$ be a rooted tree, let $v$ be a vertex of $T$, let $u$ be its parent, let $w$ be a rooted tree grafted at $v$, and let $S$ and $S'$ be the rooted trees defined by removing everything above $v$ and taking the subtree rooted at $v$, respectively. Let $\mathscr{F}_{T,t}$ and $\mathscr{E}_{T,t}$ be rational functions associated with rooted trees, and let $\mathtt{Lnr}(n)$ and $\mathtt{Crl}_n$ denote the linear tree and corolla. **Refined flow-series recursion conjecture.** There exist rational functions $\mathscr{F}_{T,t}$ such that

$$
\mathscr{F}_{T\curvearrowleft_v w,t}=\mathscr{F}_{T\curvearrowleft_u w,t}+(1-t)\mathscr{F}_{S,t}\mathscr{F}_{S',t},
$$

and such that

$$
\mathscr{F}_{\mathtt{Lnr}(n),t}=\mathscr{E}_{\mathtt{Lnr}(n),t}\qquad\text{for }n\geq1,
$$

and

$$
\mathscr{F}_{\mathtt{Crl}_n}=\frac{b(-t)^{n-2}}{(1-t)^{n-1}}\qquad\text{for }n\geq2.
$$

This conjecture seeks a parameterized refinement of the inductive identity for flow-generating series, with prescribed values on linear trees and corollas. The source provides no resolution status.

324263.title: The diagonal-word generating-function corollary for parking functions

literal.statement:
For a parking function $PF$, let $\operatorname{area}(PF)$, $\operatorname{dinv}(PF)$, and $\operatorname{ides}(PF)$ be its statistics, let $\mathcal{A}_c(\tau)$ be the set of parking functions with composition $c$ and diagonal word $\tau$, and define

$$
\mathcal{C}_c^\tau=\sum_{PF\in\mathcal{A}_c(\tau)}t^{\operatorname{area}(PF)}q^{\operatorname{dinv}(PF)}Q_{\operatorname{ides}(PF)}.
$$

**The diagonal-word generating-function conjecture.** For $b\leq a-1$ and every permutation $\tau$, one has

$$
\mathcal{C}_{a,b}^\tau+\mathcal{C}_{b+1,a-1}^\tau=q\left(\mathcal{C}_{b,a}^\tau+\mathcal{C}_{a-1,b+1}^\tau\right).
$$

This is presented as the generating-function corollary of the stronger bijection conjecture: the factor $q$ records the increase of $\operatorname{dinv}$, while preservation of the diagonal word permits the identity for each $\tau$. The source gives no resolution.

329217.title: The Fuchsian length domination conjecture for Hitchin representations

literal.statement:
Let $S$ be the surface and $\rho$ a representation in $Hit_n(S)$. A representation $\rho'$ is in the **Fuchsian locus** of $Hit_n(S)$ when it is a Fuchsian representation viewed in $Hit_n(S)$, and $l_\rho(\gamma)$ denotes the length associated with $\rho$ for $\gamma\in\Gamma$. **Fuchsian length domination conjecture.** There is some representation $\rho'$ in the Fuchsian locus of $Hit_n(S)$ such that

$$
l_{\rho}(\gamma) \geq l_{\rho'}(\gamma), \qquad \text{for any } \gamma \in \Gamma.
$$

This conjecture would compare the marked length spectrum of every Hitchin representation with that of a Fuchsian representation. The supplied passage says that the authors were unable to show that the classical collar inequality fails in $Hit_n(S)$ for any $n>2$, motivating this conjecture; no resolution is given here.

331973.title: Moment-curve extremality conjecture for crossing pairs in convex drawings

literal.statement:
Let $K_n^d$ be the complete $d$-uniform hypergraph, and let a **$d$-dimensional convex drawing** of $K_n^d$ place its $n$ vertices in convex position in $\mathbb{R}^d$, with each hyperedge represented by the simplex spanned by its vertices. The **$d$-dimensional moment curve** is the curve $\{(t,t^2,\ldots,t^d):t\in\mathbb{R}\}$.

**Moment-curve extremality conjecture.** Placing the $n$ vertices on the $d$-dimensional moment curve maximizes the number of crossing pairs of hyperedges among all $d$-dimensional convex drawings of $K_n^d$.

The conjecture concerns the extremal crossing behavior of convex drawings of complete uniform hypergraphs. The paper states that for $d>3$ it is an open problem to prove or disprove it; the exact values of the $d$-dimensional convex crossing number of $K_{2d}^d$ are likewise not known for $d>3$.

339684.title: Involution word tableau enumeration conjecture for type D

literal.statement:
Let $D_n$ be the finite Coxeter group of signed permutations with an even number of negative letters, with longest element $w_n^D$. For the identity automorphism, let $\underline{\hat{\mathcal{R}}}(w_n^D)$ denote the involution words with each occurrence of $t_1'$ replaced by $t_1$; for the automorphism $*$ interchanging $t_1$ and $t_1'$ and fixing $t_i$ for $i\in[2,n-1]$, let $\underline{\hat{\mathcal{R}}}_*(w_n^D)$ be defined analogously. Write

$$
\lambda=(n-1,n-2,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\ldots,2,1)
$$

and

$$
\mu=(n-1,n-2,\ldots,\lceil n/2\rceil-1,\lceil n/2\rceil-1,\ldots,2,1).
$$

**Involution word tableau enumeration conjecture.** If $n\geq 3$, then

$$
\left|\underline{\hat{\mathcal{R}}}(w_n^D)\right|=|\operatorname{SYT}(\lambda)|
$$

and

$$
\left|\underline{\hat{\mathcal{R}}}_*(w_n^D)\right|=|\operatorname{SYT}(\mu)|.
$$

These are proposed analogues for twisted involution words of the known type D reduced-word enumeration by standard Young tableaux. The claim is presented as an apparent analogue and no resolution is supplied in the source.

$$

This extends the corresponding bound known for cactus graphs to all connected graphs. The source gives no resolution of the conjecture.

355047.title: Sudoku number characterization of complete graphs

literal.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$. The **Sudoku number characterization.**

$$
sn(G)=n-1\quad\text{if and only if}\quad G=K_n.
$$

Here $sn(G)$ denotes the Sudoku number of $G$, and $K_n$ is the complete graph on $n$ vertices. The conjecture proposes that complete graphs are exactly the graphs attaining the general upper bound $sn(G)\leq n-1$.

356218.title: Eventual rank unimodality conjecture

literal.statement:
Let $N(m,n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ with rank $m$. **Eventual rank unimodality conjecture.** For $n\geq39$ and $0\leq m\leq n-3$, one has

$$
N(m,n)\geq N(m+1,n).
$$

By the symmetry $N(m,n)=N(-m,n)$, this gives unimodality of the rank distribution in the relevant range. The conjecture was proposed in earlier work and is proved in this paper by a Circle Method argument.
